Found the definition in the corpus (pinned working-tree source):

`snappy/snappy.cc:47-53`:
```cpp
#if !defined(SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32)
#if defined(__SSE4_2__)
#define SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32 1
#else
#define SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32 0
#endif
#endif  // !defined(SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32)
```

It is a compile-time feature macro, not a fixed constant: on x86 it expands to **1** only when `__SSE4_2__` is defined (SSE4.2 CRC32 intrinsics available), **0** otherwise. It can also be overridden externally — CMake probes the compiler and emits it via `#cmakedefine01 SNAPPY_HAVE_X86_CRC32` (`snappy/cmake/config.h.in:53`, set at `snappy/CMakeLists.txt:222`), and `snappy/README.md:78` notes MSVC users must set it manually. It guards the `#include <immintrin.h>` path (`snappy.cc:63`) and the x86 CRC32 hash implementation (`snappy.cc:169`).

ANSWER: 1 if `__SSE4_2__` is defined, 0 otherwise — it is conditionally defined, not a single constant
